- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) in recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for the next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.1) and price is trending down, model often overcorrects downward; avoid sharp drops; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- After a price spike (≥ 2% from prior peak), model frequently overestimates continuation; cap forecast peak at 1–2 days beyond the spike, then apply mean reversion toward 10–15-day moving average.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.1–0.5) and price shows no clear trend, model overfits short-term noise; use 14-day EWMA as smoothing anchor for next 7–14 days.
- Model consistently underestimates true price at 10–15 day horizon; apply 0.8–1.2% upward bias for 10–15 day forecasts, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- When sentiment is high and price is near 30-day high, model often fails to anticipate breakout; add 1–2% upward buffer for next 3–5 days if sentiment > 0.4.
- If model forecast is below 65 and sentiment is positive, avoid downward bias; assume momentum will resume; add 0.5–1.0% upward adjustment for next 5 days.
